DeployBot: INCIDENT PAGE: p99 latency breach for streaming.generate in eu-west-1. Alerting p95>1s, p99>3s, streaming stalls observed. Paging on-call. :rotating_light:
InfraBot: auto-run playbook: collect traces, enable debug logs, notify #incidents.
Aisha (SRE): I'm on the thread. first look: dashboards show a sharp jump in tail latency at 17:34 UTC, aligns with spike in cross-AZ network errors. p95 from ~120ms -> 1.3s, p99 ~4.6s. streaming stalls / client keepalive gaps 2-8s.
Dave (on-call): Taking lead. Handing off my pager to Jen in 30m if still active.
Jen (netops): I'm looking at VPC flow logs and NAT GW metrics. NAT gateway SNAT port usage at 97% for several ENIs in eu-west-1a -> a lot of connection retries. Also seeing increased TLS handshake retries in ELB logs (ELB: 502/504 counts up).
Maya (support): Customer impact: a few enterprise customers reported partial stream resets and repeated connector reconnects. Support ticket queue up for eu-west-1. No data exfil.
Aisha (SRE): Captured tcpdump from worker in eu-west-1a. snippets show multiple retransmits and fast SYN retries to model backend pool in other AZ. Looks like cross-zone routing path goes via NAT/egress and drops small TLS handshakes. Example: 
```
17:34:12.512678 IP worker-10.0.3.45.52344 > backend-10.0.7.22.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 428315 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7]
17:34:12.615712 IP worker-10.0.3.45.52344 > backend-10.0.7.22.443: Flags [S], seq 0, retransmission
```
Jen (netops): Traceroutes show asymmetric path: traffic from eu-west-1a to backends in eu-west-1b goes through a NAT TGW that is advertising next-hop in a different AZ. Route table changed ~17:30 UTC (probable config churn). Pulling CloudTrail now.
Dave (on-call): Quick mitigation ideas: 1) Force AZ-local routing for streaming via ENI policy on workers; 2) Fallback to regional non-streaming endpoint (disable streaming for critical tenants) to avoid long-lived TLS state; 3) Add temporary NAT capacity / replace NATGW. Which is fastest?
Aisha (SRE): Option 2 fastest for immediate customer experience: flip traffic for top-10 enterprise tenants to non-streaming generation endpoint (stateless, short requests). I can push a canary config in 2-3min.
Maya (support): Agree. Start with top customers (account ids listed in support runbook). Notify them of failover.
Jen (netops): For infra fix: increasing NATGW provisioning may take minutes; creating new per-AZ NAT gateway and updating route table *should* cut cross-zone hops. Preparing change now but will require careful rollout.
DeployBot: Deploy request queued: feature-toggle streaming -> non-streaming for tenanted routing. Approve with :thumbsup:.
Dave (on-call): Approved. Aisha proceed. Jen, proceed with NATGW per-AZ after we stabilize. Keep me posted.
Aisha (SRE): Pushing toggle for top-10 now. Rolling in canary -> 20% -> 100% for those tenants. Logs: keepalive gaps drop to <200ms for canary clients.
Maya (support): Sent proactive notifications to affected customers, noted failover to non-stream endpoint and ETA for full fix. No legal/regulatory impact.
Jen (netops): Route change in progress: creating NAT gateway in eu-west-1a, updating subnet route to prefer local NAT. Will monitor flow logs for cross-AZ hops.
InfraBot: change submitted: create-natgw eu-west-1a (id: nat-abc123).
Aisha (SRE): Canary metrics look good. p95 back ~180ms, p99 down to ~900ms for the impacted tenants. Streaming clients still show a small percentage doing retries (some client-side backoff issues).
Dave (on-call): Good. Next steps: keep canary running 30m, then roll to all affected tenants. Jen to confirm route stability and NATGW metrics <80% usage. Postmortem owner: Aisha, timeline + root cause: route churn + NAT port exhaustion causing TLS handshake retransmits and streaming stalls.
Jen (netops): NATGW in eu-west-1a active, port utilization down to 42%. Flow logs show <1% cross-AZ packets now. CloudTrail shows a config change from a housekeeping job at 17:29 that updated TGW route table - investigating who/what triggered it.
Maya (support): Customers acknowledged, some prefer permanent regional pinning. Capturing requests.
Aisha (SRE): Collecting all logs/traces/pcaps for postmortem. Saved tcpdump, ELB logs, worker traces. If anyone has other traces drop them here.
Dave (on-call): Thanks all. I'll hand back to primary oncall after cooldown. Incident: mitigation successful, partial customer impact for ~18 minutes, elevated p99 for ~22 minutes. Marking status: mitigated.
InfraBot: Incident ticket updated: status=mitigated, owner=Aisha, severity=SEV2, start=1769204832, mitigated=1769205145.
Maya (support): Opening follow-up thread for customer comms and compensation notes.
Aisha (SRE): Postmortem will include recommended guardrails: prevent TGW route churn without approval, auto-scale NAT or prefer per-AZ NAT, and a streaming fallback toggle for enterprise tenants.
Dave (on-call): Closing handoff. Good job team. :tada:
